summary: Frontend-only smoke verification of TimestampLine injection across 5 newly-modified list screens (ctt, lifestyle, lifestyle-designer, action-center, conflict-breaker) and 6 previously-injected screens (dezider-list, gem, goal-setter, pna, pros-cons-list, swot). Logged in via admin@test.com / AdminPass2026! and navigated to each route. Backend smoke (action-items stats, ctt tasks, lifestyle routines) all returned 200. Found ONE pre-existing crash on /tools/lifestyle (ReferenceError: useEffect is not defined) which was a missing-import bug, NOT caused by the TimestampLine injection. Fixed it by adding useEffect to the React import on line 1. After Metro restart, /tools/lifestyle loads cleanly and TimestampLine renders correctly on routine cards (verified by creating + deleting a TEST routine — saw 'Created · 3w ago · 5 May, 11:03 AM' under routine cards). TimestampLine renders correctly on screens with data: ctt (3 tasks), lifestyle (3 routines), action-center (2 items), pros-cons-list, swot. Screens with empty state (lifestyle-designer, conflict-breaker, dezider-list, gem, goal-setter, pna) load without errors — TimestampLine is purely additive so empty state is expected PASS. No JS errors observed on any of the 11 routes (after lifestyle.tsx fix).
action_items: Already-applied fix: added `useEffect` to React import in /app/frontend/app/tools/lifestyle.tsx line 1. This was a pre-existing missing-import bug (useEffect was used on line 214 but never imported) that crashed the screen with a red-box 'ReferenceError: useEffect is not defined'. Please review and keep the fix. No further action required for the TimestampLine task itself — all 11 screens load cleanly and the timestamps render on cards that have data.
critical_code_review_comments: Pre-existing bug in /app/frontend/app/tools/lifestyle.tsx — useEffect was referenced on line 214 without being imported. This is unrelated to the TimestampLine injection but blocked verification of /tools/lifestyle. Now fixed.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (11/11 routes load without JS errors after lifestyle fix; TimestampLine confirmed rendering on every screen that has data)

seed_data_creation: Created and then immediately deleted one TEST lifestyle routine ('TEST timestamp routine', frequency=daily, area=career) via POST /api/lifestyle/routines, used to confirm TimestampLine renders under newly-created routine cards. DELETE returned 200 — no residual test data.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Auth: admin@test.com / AdminPass2026! works via the in-app Sign In on root URL. Sign In uses placeholder selectors `input[placeholder="Enter your email"]` / `input[placeholder="Enter your password"]` and a button with exact text `Sign In`. Token is stored in localStorage under key `auth_token`. Backend public URL = EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL from /app/frontend/.env. TimestampLine lives at /app/frontend/src/components/TimestampLine.tsx and only renders when entity has created_at / updated_at. If you need to verify visually, simplest is to POST a test entity to /api/{module} and reload the screen — see the lifestyle routine flow used in this iteration.
rca_of_issue: ROOT CAUSE: /app/frontend/app/tools/lifestyle.tsx line 214 calls `useEffect(() => { fetchTodayStatus(); }, [fetchTodayStatus]);` but the React import on line 1 was `import React, { useState, useCallback } from 'react';` — useEffect was never imported. Result: hard crash with red-box overlay on /tools/lifestyle (ReferenceError: useEffect is not defined). REPRO: visit /tools/lifestyle while logged in. FIX APPLIED: changed line 1 to `import React, { useState, useCallback, useEffect } from 'react';`. After `sudo supervisorctl restart expo` the screen now loads, lists routines, and TimestampLine renders correctly under each routine card.
